The Supplier will normally provide the Services personally. If the Supplier cannot attend agreed work, the Supplier may propose another person to provide it instead. title: Off-payroll working: Company determines, rules do not apply
subject: services

all.body:
The Company is a medium or large client under the off-payroll working rules in Chapter 10 of Part 2 of the Income Tax (Earnings and Pensions) Act 2003, so it is responsible for deciding whether those rules apply to this engagement. It has taken reasonable care in deciding, and gave a status determination statement with its reasons to the Operative and the Supplier on {{offpayroll.sds_date}}. Its conclusion is that the rules do not apply.

On that basis the Company pays the fees to the Supplier without deducting income tax or National Insurance contributions. If the Company issues a new status determination statement, the tax treatment of the fees changes from the date that statement gives, and the parties will record the change in a written variation.

The person responsible at the Company for status determinations under this agreement is {{offpayroll.responsible}}.

title: Off-payroll working: Company determines, rules apply (Company is fee-payer)
subject: services

all.body:
The Company is a medium or large client under the off-payroll working rules in Chapter 10 of Part 2 of the Income Tax (Earnings and Pensions) Act 2003, so it is responsible for deciding whether those rules apply to this engagement. It has taken reasonable care in deciding, and gave a status determination statement with its reasons to the Operative and the Supplier on {{offpayroll.sds_date}}. Its conclusion is that the rules apply.

The Company contracts directly with the Supplier, so it is the deemed employer (the fee-payer). For each payment of fees it will work out the deemed direct payment to the Operative as the rules require, deduct income tax and employee National Insurance contributions from it through PAYE, and pay employer National Insurance contributions and any Apprenticeship Levy itself. It will pay the Supplier the balance of the fees, together with VAT on the full fee where the Supplier is registered. Student and postgraduate loan repayments are not deducted.

The Supplier must give the Company the information it needs to do this, including the Operative's National Insurance number, and tell it promptly of any change. Being treated as employed for tax under these rules does not on its own make the Operative an employee or worker of the Company under employment law.

The person responsible at the Company for status determinations under this agreement is {{offpayroll.responsible}}.

title: Off-payroll working: small client, the Supplier decides
subject: services

all.body:
The Company is a small client under the off-payroll working rules, so it does not decide the Operative's status for tax. The Supplier is responsible for deciding whether the intermediaries rules in Chapter 8 of Part 2 of the Income Tax (Earnings and Pensions) Act 2003 apply to this engagement and, if they do, for accounting to HMRC for the tax and National Insurance contributions due. The Company pays the fees without deduction.

The Company will confirm its size if the Supplier or the Operative asks. It will check its size before each tax year and tell the Supplier in writing as soon as it expects to stop being small. From the tax year in which the Company is no longer small, it will decide the Operative's status under Chapter 10 and give a status determination statement, and the tax terms of this agreement will be reviewed.

The person responsible for the status assessment under this agreement is {{offpayroll.responsible}}.

title: Off-payroll working: disagreeing with a status determination
subject: services

all.body:
If the Operative or the Supplier disagrees with the status determination statement, they may tell the Company in writing, with their reasons, at any time before the final payment of fees for this engagement. Representations go to {{offpayroll.disagreement_contact}}.

The Company will consider them and, within the statutory 45 days of receiving them, either confirm its conclusion with its reasons or give a new status determination statement stating the date from which the new conclusion applies. The existing statement continues to apply until then.

The Supplier is responsible for its own corporation tax, VAT and company filings, and for paying the Operative and any other Supplier Personnel, including operating PAYE on any salary it pays them. The Company is not responsible for the Supplier's taxes beyond the duties the off-payroll working rules place on it.

The Supplier must keep records that show how fees received under this agreement have been paid out, and must co-operate with any reasonable request from the Company or HMRC about the tax treatment of this engagement.

Each party is responsible for loss or damage it causes through its own negligence or its breach of this agreement.

The Supplier's total liability to the Company under or in connection with this agreement in each contract year is limited to {{liability.cap}}. This limit does not apply to loss that the insurance this agreement requires covers, or would have covered if it had been in place, to breach of the confidentiality or data protection terms, or to deliberate wrongdoing.

Nothing in this agreement limits or excludes either party's liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, for fraud, or for anything else the law does not allow to be limited or excluded.

Either party may end this agreement by giving the other {{notice.period}} written notice. Agreed work that falls within the notice period goes ahead unless the parties agree otherwise, or it is cancelled under the cancellation terms.

Either party may end this agreement straight away by written notice if the other:

- commits a serious breach of it, or a breach that it does not put right within a reasonable time after being asked to;
- becomes insolvent, is made bankrupt or sequestrated, or stops trading.

The Company may also end this agreement, or any agreed work, straight away by written notice if a licence the Services need is suspended, revoked or expires, or if screening or right-to-work checks are not satisfactory.

When this agreement ends, the Supplier must return all property and information of the Company and its clients, and the Company will pay for Services properly provided up to the end date. The terms on confidentiality, data protection, liability and tax continue after it ends.
